target_translation: The written bytes are the writer's private deep copy (owned, no other view), but in Rust the PS info's raw_params_ hold OwnedParseTree (RULEBOOK 0.12) whose bytes are never written in place (api/09 §4 P2), so the owned write is expressed as copy-modify-repoint inside the tree's private arena. The source has two kinds: (a) a request parse node - assign_fixed_raw_params (:397) <- ob_ps_cache.cpp:477 with the fast-parser raw_params_ (ob_sql.cpp:975): `OwnedParseTree::new_with(src_node, |root, arena| { let mut ret: ObResult = Ok(()); if NEG_PARAM == flag { let s = root.str_bytes(); if s.first() != Some(&b'-') { ret = Err(OB_ERR_UNEXPECTED); log_warn!(ret, "expected neg sign here", ..); } else { let mut tmp_pos = 1usize; while tmp_pos < s.len() && isspace(s[tmp_pos] as c_int) { tmp_pos += 1; } let n = s.len() - (tmp_pos - 1); match arena.parser_alloc((n + 1) as i64) { None => ret = Err(OB_ALLOCATE_MEMORY_FAILED), Some(buf) => { buf[..n].copy_from_slice(&s[tmp_pos - 1..]); buf[0] = b'-'; let buf: &[u8] = buf; root.set_str_value(&buf[..n]); } } } } ret })` (api/09 §2.2.5, §6 ex.7; parser_alloc zero-fills, so buf[n] keeps the NUL of the C++ deep copy; set_str_value writes str_value_ and str_len_ = n together, the view of the C++ pointer advance :372-373); (b) another PS info's raw_params_ - deep_copy_fixed_raw_params (:417) <- ObPsStmtInfo::deep_copy (:461): the source is already an OwnedParseTree, which offers no ParseNode handle, so `src_tree.try_clone()` and copy flag_ (:360); the NEG_PARAM fix-up is skipped because it is a no-op on an already fixed tree (first byte '-', next byte non-space: the scan stops at tmp_pos = 1, writes '-' over '-' and advances by 0). Both branches then push the owned param (:376). The ObPCParam + ParseNode block allocation (:352-358) becomes the construction of that owned param; its OB_ALLOCATE_MEMORY_FAILED branch maps to new_with's / try_clone's error. ObPCParam therefore needs two forms (request ParseNode<'p> vs OwnedParseTree) or an enum - decided by its c03 row (ObPCParam::node_, ob_plan_cache_util.h:250), which also fixes this function's parameter type. The new_with closure needs both arguments tied to one lifetime (`for<'p> FnOnce(ParseNode<'p>, &'p ParseArena)`), which api/09 §2.2.5 does not state (reported).
evidence: param->node_ is a fresh deep copy into the PS info's own allocator: block alloc :352 [allocation-guard :352-353], deep_copy_parse_node :359 copies str_value_ into a new NUL-terminated buffer (parse_node.c:114-123); write :371 puts '-' right before the first non-space char after the sign (scan :366-370), then advances the view :372-373; published afterwards by raw_params_.push_back :376; two callers with different sources: assign_fixed_raw_params :381-405 (call :397) <- ob_ps_cache.cpp:477 with info_ctx.raw_params_ = the request's fp_result_.raw_params_ (ob_sql.cpp:975), and deep_copy_fixed_raw_params :408-425 (call :417) <- ObPsStmtInfo::deep_copy :461 with another PS info's raw_params_ (already fixed, flag_ copied :360); readers later: PS execution across sessions/threads ob_sql.cpp:1604-1608,1705-1823 (hence OwnedParseTree); C++ would dereference a NULL str_value_ at :364 for a NEG_PARAM node with str_len_ 0 (the deep copy skips empty strings, parse_node.c:114); s.first() turns that into OB_ERR_UNEXPECTED (not reachable for NEG_PARAM nodes)

target_translation: Bytes borrowed from the parse tree (RULEBOOK §2.4: 拷贝、修改、改指; api/09 §3.1): `let node0 = action_node.child(0).unwrap();` (NULL handled at :602-605) `let src = node0.str_bytes(); let mut name: &[u8] = src;` `if !src.is_empty() { match ParseArena::from_arena(self.params_.allocator_).parser_alloc(src.len() as i64) { None => { ret = Err(OB_ALLOCATE_MEMORY_FAILED); break; } Some(buf) => { buf.copy_from_slice(src); let mut w = ObStringWriter::with_length(buf, src.len() as i32); let _ = ObCharset::casedn_string(CS_TYPE_UTF8MB4_GENERAL_CI, &mut w); name = w.into_string(); node0.set_str_value(name); } } }` then `if ob_fail!(ret = item.name_.assign(name)) { break; }` as before. casedn_string is the overloads.tsv name (overloads.tsv:1288) of casedn(const ObCollationType, ObString &) (ob_charset.h:663); plain `casedn` is the 5-argument char* overload (ob_charset.h:508). Its parameter is `&mut ObStringWriter<'_>` because the callee uses the ObString as a write buffer - it rewrites the bytes in place and set_length()s (ob_charset.cpp:1842-1850) - which is RULEBOOK §2.5's "ObString 当写缓冲用 -> ObStringWriter" row (api/06 §2.1.2 has set_length/ptr_mut); an explicit rule for in-place `ObString &` parameters is queued as an amendment. params_.allocator_ is the statement arena the parser used (ob_sql.cpp:2055), so the copy has the node's 'p. No other view needs repointing (pretag local:view: the view is local, the bytes are the node's).
